DR085 PROOF085 L:driver-noise-basis.claim: The prescribed nonzero quotient H_W is separable and infinite-dimensional and has a real orthonormal basis of compact smooth representatives whose W-evaluations are independent standard real Gaussians.
DR085 PROOF085 L:driver-noise-basis.reason: Reconstructed from E:driver-test-continuity: |<F,G>| bounded by |K|Gamma(K-K) 2L^(1-a)/(1-a) times the time sup-L2 norms, so rational-box step-plus-mollifier collections are uniformly dense, giving separability without injectivity. Infinite dimensionality follows from Q_sp = int Gamma(dy) int q(x)q(x-y)dx >= |B_{L+1}|Gamma(B_L)>0 for q>=1 on B_{2L+1}, the tensor identity ||tau tensor q||^2 = Q_sp ||tau||_a^2, and the positive Laplace factorization with v' = lambda v - tau forcing tau=0. Gram-Schmidt on a countable dense real collection, discarding quotient-null residuals, gives compact smooth representatives; the isonormal property gives E[g_j g_k]=delta_jk and joint Gaussian factorization gives independence. Gamma=0 is handled separately and no H_W-valued Gaussian is introduced.

DR086 PROOF086 L:driver-covariance-coeff.claim: H_{j,R}(t,x)=zeta_R(x) int_{u>0}|t-u|^{-a}(Gamma*f_j)(u,x-u term) is smooth real, spatially supported in B_{2R} with bounded mixed derivatives, satisfies the literal covariance row E[W_C(zeta_R F)g_j]=int H_{j,R}F, and depends only on the H_W class on t>=0.
DR086 PROOF086 L:driver-covariance-coeff.reason: The substitution v=t-u confines v to a bounded interval and y to a compact set for compact (t,x), so local Radon mass and local |v|^{-a} integrability move all derivatives onto the compact smooth f_j, giving smoothness and bounded derivatives; zeta_R then gives support B_{2R}. The isonormal covariance and absolute Fubini give the row for compact real tests, extended to complex wave tests through the common-support raw approximations of P:actual-wave-form. Class invariance is established by distributional vanishing on t>0, smoothness, and continuity at zero. The mask stays after convolution, matching downstream use.

DR087 PROOF087 L:driver-gain-localizatio.claim: A_j(I)=int_I S(-t)B(H_{j,R}(t))S(t)dt has gain E_r->E_{r+1}, E_s-adjoint gain E_{2s-r-1}->E_{2s-r}, hence both E_{s-gamma}->E; with chi=1 on B_{2R+T+1}, D_chi A_j(I)=A_j(I)=A_j(I)D_chi; and E[g_j ell_R(I;z,w)]=<A_j(I)z,w>_E.
DR087 PROOF087 L:driver-gain-localizatio.reason: For r chosen so the second entry of B(H) is a bounded multiplier H^r->H^r; compact smooth coefficient gives t-uniform boundedness, and each Fourier entry is bounded by a fixed C_T, so the Bochner integrand is strongly continuous with bounded operator norm and integration gives gain one. The actual E_s pair identifies the dual of E_r with E_{2s-r}=E_{1-r}, so A* gains E_{2s-r-1}->E_{2s-r}; choosing r=s+gamma-1 gives domain E_{s-gamma} and codomain E_{s+1-gamma} subset E since gamma<1. The two identity localizations follow from the full two-entry finite-propagation cone argument (both displacement and velocity), H_{j,R} supported in B_{2R}, output in B_{2R+T}, and chi=1 on a neighborhood of B_{2R+T+1}. The covariance row uses the actual physical-adjoint identity together with DR086.

DR089 PROOF089 L:driver-dominated-tails.claim: For 0<=T_N<=B with positive compact B in S_m (m>=1) and T_N->0 weakly, ||T_N||->0 and Tr T_N^m->0.
DR089 PROOF089 L:driver-dominated-tails.reason: For unit x, x=Qx+(I-Q)x with Q a finite spectral projection of B, the inequality bounds <T_N x,x> by 2||QT_NQ||+2||(I-Q)B(I-Q)||; weak convergence drives the finite matrix QT_NQ to zero and letting eps->0 gives norm convergence. Compact positive order gives lambda_j(T_N)<=lambda_j(B), norm convergence gives lambda_j(T_N)->0 pointwise, and dominated summation against the summable spectrum lambda_j(B)^m proves the trace limit. The proof explicitly avoids asserting operator-power order T_N^m<=B^m.

DR090 PROOF090 L:driver-gaussian-tail-av.claim: For finitely many compact Z_l with V_out,V_in in S_{q/2} and independent standard real g_l, E||sum g_l Z_l||_{S_q}^q <= (q-1)^(q/2)(Tr V_out^(q/2)+Tr V_in^(q/2))/2.
DR090 PROOF090 L:driver-gaussian-tail-av.reason: Finite-rank compression gives output variance <= Q_k V_out Q_k (difference equals sum Q_k Z_l(I-Q_k)Z_l* Q_k >=0) and the input analog, then the finite-dimensional P:finite-gaussian-matrix bound is applied and passed to the compact operators via norm-Lipschitz singular values plus Fatou over singular values and probability. Measurability follows by finite-coordinate continuity. No infinite Gaussian series or S_q Bochner convergence is required.

DR092 PROOF092 L:driver-holder-limit.claim: X_N(t)=X_N((0,t)) converges in L^p(Omega;C^theta([0,T];B(E))) for all finite p>=1 in a separable closed path span, limit starts at zero and has compact values at all times on one event, and for large even q_0 the C^theta L^q norm is <= C sqrt(q) uniformly over even q>=q_0 and the basis.
DR092 PROOF092 L:driver-holder-limit.reason: The strict choice theta<eta<beta and even q_0 with q_0 gamma>d and beta-eta-1/q_0>0 is verified. The uniform Schatten-step bound from the retained Gaussian estimate and the fixed S_{q_0} cutoff gives L^q increments <= C sqrt(q)|t-u|^beta; the finite-maximum bound gives D_n <= 2^(n/q)C sqrt(q)(T2^{-n})^beta, and the geometric sum closes with gap beta-eta-1/q_0>0. The dyadic sum controls the C^eta norm for zero-start continuous paths; fixed-grid-then-mesh convergence with the uniform C^eta bound proves sup-norm Cauchy; deterministic interpolation and scalar Holder prove C^theta Cauchy; Lyapunov covers arbitrary p. The limit lies in the C^theta-closed span of the countable deterministic Lipschitz paths A_j(0,.), and an a.s. C^theta-convergent subsequence gives compact values at all times on one path event.

DR093 PROOF093 P:actual-operator-driver.claim: There is a same-noise compact operator path M_R with finite-path convergence E:driver-path-convergence in every L^p C^theta B(E); centered Gaussian, starts at zero, compact at all times on one event; fixed Schwartz raw rows equal ell_R((0,t);z,w) in L^2 including long-interval additivity; basis indistinguishability; (E||M_R||^p)^(1/p)<=C sqrt(p) and exponential square-integrability; complexification and fixed admissible even Schatten indices.
DR093 PROOF093 P:actual-operator-driver.reason: Assembled from 085-092 on the original probability space; evaluation at fixed t agrees with the interval limit by uniqueness in probability; every continuous functional of the finite Gaussian path sum converges in L^2 to a centered Gaussian, giving the Gaussian path property; four real pair identities give the sesquilinear row. Basis indistinguishability uses a fixed countable dense Schwartz collection and rational times plus boundedness and path continuity, so only a countable null-set union is needed, distinguishing it from an uncountable raw-event intersection. The norm bound uses, for each p, an even q with q>=max(p,q_0) and q<=p+q_0+2<=(q_0+3)p, yielding C sqrt(p); the exponential bound follows from E Y^(2m)<=(C1 sqrt(2m))^(2m) and m!>=(m/e)^m, giving series terms bounded by (2ecC1^2)^m for c<1/(2eC1^2), with C1=0 handled trivially. Path moments are B(E) norms, not arbitrary Schatten-valued or endpoint claims.

APP-TAIL-INTERVAL.claim: Current 088/091 use the actual Fourier/Bessel columns, both compact summable envelopes, the retained Gaussian average and vanishing traces to prove same-space tail Cauchy convergence, row/additivity and fixed-interval compact Gaussianity.
APP-TAIL-INTERVAL.reason: 088 proves both actual weighted variance directions (V_out and V_in) bounded by b_I D_gamma^2 with both localizations by P_chi and positive tails strongly tending to zero under b_I B_out/B_in. 091 then, for admissible even q with q gamma>d, puts the envelopes in S_{q/2}; DR089 gives Tr T_{out/in,N}^(q/2)->0; DR090 gives sup_{M>N} E||Y_{N,M}||_{S_q}^q->0; this is genuine L^q(B(E)) Cauchy convergence, not merely a uniform moment bound. The limit is taken in the separable operator-norm closed span of the countable deterministic A_j(I), is compact-valued, centered Gaussian on the original space, and has the literal fixed Schwartz row identity plus exact additivity over finite partitions; endpoint changes of long-interval indicators have zero raw norm. Common compact summable envelopes are the decisive ingredient, avoiding the strong-convergence-only counterexample.

APP-PATH-VERSION.claim: Fixed-grid-then-mesh convergence and deterministic/probability interpolation produce a strongly measurable separable-span C^theta path, compact at all times on one event, preserving every fixed raw row and basis indistinguishability.
APP-PATH-VERSION.reason: This is exactly the 092/093 join. Fixed-grid pointwise convergence from 091 is combined with the uniform dyadic C^eta bound; the mesh is then refined; deterministic C^theta interpolation and scalar probability Holder close the Cauchy property in the separable C^theta-closed span of the countable A_j(0,.) paths. An a.s. C^theta-convergent subsequence is uniform in operator norm, so compact values hold at all times on one path event. Rows are preserved by uniqueness in probability at fixed times, and basis indistinguishability follows from a countable dense collection plus continuity, avoiding an uncountable null-set intersection.
